items.reason: DCSZ11 is given alone in "Phase 1a Dose Escalation Monotherapy" and with pembrolizumab in the other arms that GBM patients can enter ("in combination with pembrolizumab in Part 2"). If pembrolizumab is a second investigational agent (see below), DCSZ11 is experimental_combination in the combination arms. The manual gives no rule for choosing one role when roles differ by arm. Either role keeps it a candidate.

"Patients with known driver mutations/genomic aberrations (i.e., EGFR, B-Raf proto-oncogene mutation V600E ...) are not eligible" is an exclusion in the NSCLC expansion cohort, not an entry requirement. It does not change any derived outcome (not matched, and any_molecular_selection is already true from MSS-CRC).
Same NSCLC-cohort exclusion of known driver mutations. It is an exclusion criterion, not a required biomarker, and it does not affect outcomes.
Same NSCLC-cohort exclusion ("neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase [NRTK] gene fusions ... are not eligible"). It does not affect outcomes.

items.reason: Same NSCLC-cohort exclusion. It does not affect outcomes.

Pembrolizumab is not given in every arm (there is a DCSZ11 monotherapy arm), is not GBM standard of care, and its combination with DCSZ11 is the tested regimen ("determine DCSZ11 Phase 1b doses in combination with pembrolizumab"), so rule 3 does not apply. Against that, it is a fixed approved partner whose own dose is not studied, which could be read as backbone. No ruling covers this.

As above. In GBM patients (Phase 1a Part 2 only) pembrolizumab is not background therapy, so it counts as a second investigational agent. This makes the trial contain an approved-drug candidate (origin category 2), which is why XL should confirm.

Under the non-candidate-partner convention proposed for this batch, the only non-candidate antitumour drugs in experimental arms are the SOC partners in "Phase 1b Standard of Care" (doxorubicin for sarcoma, tebentafusp for uveal melanoma). If XL treats pembrolizumab as backbone, or lists co-candidates too, coder B's list is right.

note: Key decision for XL: whether pembrolizumab is a candidate (it changes the trial's origin group to repurposing_containing). GBM patients can enter only Phase 1a (DCSZ11 alone, or DCSZ11 + pembrolizumab); doxorubicin and tebentafusp are in non-GBM cohorts. any_molecular_selection is true only from the MSS-CRC expansion cohort (TMB_MMR enrichment, agreed), which does not apply to GBM patients. GBM is named in inclusion notes, so it is a basket under D27B. The combination_partners convention is the same open question as in NCT05734560 and NCT06356883.
